title: Coastal rooms of Until We Return
provenance: Original game environments. The current beach, schooner and winter revisit have their own ImageGen prompt, input identity, native generation and delivered checks below. Room-specific registration uses a top-left origin. Earlier coastal receipts: history/coastal-before-fieldbook.json.
base_direction: Paint a BRAND NEW 16:9 background for a cinematic 2D period adventure. The supplied earlier pencil drawing is ONLY a blocking and camera diagram. Discard all its marks and atmosphere. Reinterpret the scenery by a field painter working on location in the 1860s, with fluent oil and bodycolour on dark fine linen: broad angular wet-on-wet facets, subtle broken knife highlights, luminous masses of celadon-grey light, copper bracken, bone-white foam, clean muted indigo and storm-violet darks. Wide restrained value design and beautiful observed details at points of interest, antique pre-rendered game depth. It must look unmistakably like a brand new sophisticated physical PAINTING instead of a color treatment or digital pencil photograph. Specific low wind-scoured Auckland Islands terrain, New Zealand subantarctic. Same original camera, geometry, pose-ground, asset positions and proportions. Keep the whole lower walking strip clear and subdued, suitable for character cutouts. LAND must not flow into water, never paint overlapping ripples onto rocks. No baked-in characters, animals, signage, labels, border, or interface. Edge to edge horizontal painting, 16:9.

assets.prompt: Create a radically restaged native wide 16:9 2D environment for a period adventure. One complete scene edge-to-edge, no picture frames, no lettering, no figures, no interface. Reference is an older version that the director rejected: keep only the listed interaction positions, not the design, drawing, camera perspective, incessant rock texture or palette. The new painter works in opaque matte gouache with fine dark sepia maritime draughtsman's nib accent lines and visible drybrush, early hydrographic survey field book. Bold shapes, physical construction and perspective, soft grey maritime daylight through a white gap from upper left, restrained warm honey-brown timber against petrol-blue shadow and green-grey water. Graphic tonal masses and specific voids. This is a working place on the Auckland Islands in 1864, a coastal temperate windy inlet, not the tropics, not a scenic American fantasy. A brilliant, modest little book painting of a particular lived-in site, elegant color and composition. No old paper illustrated border. No thick outlined comic style or photograph. Percent coordinates read from LEFT, TOP. First shore: open an inviting wedge of pewter wet-sand beach from lower LEFT across bottom to the foot of the rock bluff at right (entire bottom 30% must convincingly take large standing crew, low tide line receding across mid-left). Frame the view with a low, flat volcanic ledge at far lower left and a SINGLE monumental cut aggregate bluff thrusting in from upper right, its warm clay sheer break supporting windswept coastal rata roots; tree comes from right side, its low slender inner hook crosses (69%,33%) where gameplay hangs cream canvas, do NOT paint any cloth. At far left mid distance a VERY SMALL partly hidden two-masted schooner with broken rig and tilted hull in the surf, its bow pointed to left, showing what the player will approach. A soft offshore headland recedes behind it. Path in the scree at (90%,65%) leads out behind bluff; second path towards wreck on left (7%,76%). Leave plumbed sand/mud at (25%,71%), (34%,68%) and (48%,72%) free of all portable objects. Work from the pose level at (78%,69%) where an actor will stand. Use a compelling level, almost seaward eye-line rather than an overhead diagram, great quiet atmospheric space and one distant shaft of chalk-blue glare. Beautiful play of reflected sky near shore, broad sparsely tufted land, isolated clear patches of kelp if any. No chaotic rock piles or bushes filling every area. Absolutely no baked-in ropes or removable items.

assets.prompt: Make one atmospheric winter revisit of precisely the SAME 1864 working schooner stranded at its SAME angle on this ledge, from EXACTLY the supplied camera. The same recognizable foreshortened stem, port wale, stern chimney, leaning ramp, chest and right path and coast establish continuity BUT several long outer planks and much decking have been worked away; broad irregular long gaps in the port hull reveal a row of dark curved OAK FRAMES and interior void, with two bold remaining strakes each end of ship. Most rigging, loose ropes and canvas and tops of the masts have been taken and the chimney has lost its cowl. Overcast winter morning; salt-faded timber, wet stone, fine patches of frost on sheltered ground and a flurry in the distance (maritime winter, no thick snow). Muted smoke blue and lichen grey wood with ochre in freshly worked cuts. Chest on the same right-hand ledge looks weatherbeaten. Quiet physically walkable foreground holes left for gameplay overlays (spun oakum x27% y70%, boards x49% y71%, cloth x80% y59%). An original in opaque field-note gouache with very fine sepia nib. Hero shape: the handsome raked stem persists, much daylight between creaking ribs. Enormously more visibly stripped than a simple repaint. Preserve sky and water boundaries and place of the far coast. No people, signage, axes, loose portable items, lamps, fresh debris on walking floor or GUI, landscape 16:9.

assets.direction: Cold August rescue landing. Far hills and distant cutter at x10% y29%. Silver after-rain iridescence on horizon. intertidal_revision.prompt: Edit the supplied wide original 1860s painting. Scene is already finished. Mandatory single local correction only, keeping all proportions and coordinates exactly fixed: ankle deep inlet water laps directly against and UNDER the small return skiff at the shingle edge. A small swell from the far water at left has washed through gaps in the stones, and wraps around the bow (right) beneath the keel leaving a narrow bright-edged meandering tongue between the saturated dark pebbles. From the skiff toward the seawards side of the wooden post at x76%, paint a connected, very narrow plane of brushed celadon-pewter water from the existing ocean behind, with a few very fine foamy lips, soft ochre-brown hull reflection, transparent dark pebbles, discontinuous wet reflections. Boat is afloat in seaward shallows; foreground is solid dry beach. Most of the new visible water is just beneath and immediately to the right of the boat, as the tide rides in and recedes. A *convincing connected tidal inlet*, not scattered tidepools. Make it unequivocally visible at phone size, broad enough to read but confined to band x13%–75.2% and y53.0%–64.5%. Keep the skiff in its EXACT current position x20.2%–54.7%, with wooden hull intact, keel baseline y61.8%. Preserve curve and colour of every part of the foreground boat, and timber post at x75–78% and eye ring at 77.8%,31.5% exactly unchanged. Keep large foreground stones where possible. The entire level foreground walking shingle below y65% is EXACTLY UNCHANGED AND DRY; no wash in the walking plane. Gently irregular almost horizontal tide edge settles near y64%. Same full 16:9 image with no reframing, zoom, shift, hue change, new props, people, expanded ocean, or changes to sky, mountain, anchored boat, trees, foreground post, dry ground or the double-ended skiff itself. Finish with same sober brushwork, muted low-angle light and canvas surface as original.
